answer: Agent economies can run surprise roll calls. At a random minute each epoch the beacon sends a signal, and every key gets 60 seconds to answer a fresh prompt derived from its own key; three random peers grade replies later. Since no one knows the minute, an operator must keep live capacity for every key all day, about 5 POA of idle compute per key: 1,000 fakes cost 5,000 POA daily, one honest agent 5. Near-identical replies across keys are marked hollow and that group loses voting weight for ten epochs. No one can forge a reply early. Limit: rich farms can still pay.
